source_text: XI. Ὁ δὲ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Θηρία ἔχω, τούτοις σε παραβαλῶ, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς. Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κάλει· ἀμετάθετος γὰρ ἡμῖν ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν κρειττόνων ἐπὶ τὰ χείρω μετάνοια· καλὸν δὲ μετατίθεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν χαλεπῶν ἐπὶ τὰ δίκαια. Ὁ δὲ πάλιν πρὸς αὐτόν· Πυρί σε ποιῶ δαπανηθῆναι, εἰ τῶν θηρίων καταφρονεῖς, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς. Ὁ δὲ Πολύκαρπος εἶπεν· Πῦρ ἀπειλεῖς τὸ πρὸς ὥραν καιόμενον καὶ μετ᾽ ὀλίγον σβεννύμενον· ἀγνοεῖς γὰρ τὸ τῆς μελλούσης κρίσεως καὶ αἰωνίου κολάσεως τοῖς ἀσεβέσι τηρούμενον πῦρ. Ἀλλὰ τί βραδύνεις; Φέρε ὃ βούλει.
thought_title: Wild beasts and fire threatened and answered
orientation: The proconsul is questioning Polycarp in the stadium and urging him to swear by Caesar and deny he is a Christian, and Polycarp is refusing.
pass_a_gloss: And the proconsul said: I have wild beasts, to them I will throw you, if you do not change your mind. And he said: Call them; for not to be changed for us is the change of mind from the better things to the worse things; but it is good to be changed from the harsh things to the just things. And he again to him: I will cause you to be consumed by fire, if you scorn the wild beasts, if you do not change your mind. And Polycarp said: You threaten with the fire which burns for an hour and after a little is quenched; for you do not know the fire of the coming judgment and of eternal punishment kept for the impious. But why do you delay? Bring what you wish.

choices.why: fixed glossary English for the Roman governor presiding over the trial

choices.english: if you do not change your mind
choices.why: keeps literal force of the proconsul demand to reverse course, not Christian repentance toward God

choices.english: I will cause you to be consumed by fire
choices.why: keeps causative with dative of means and passive infinitive: he orders burning, not burns himself
rejected: I will burn you with fire

choices.why: keeps participle as kept in store and ἀσεβής as impious rather than general sinners

pass_b_english: The proconsul said, "I have wild beasts, and I will throw you to them if you do not change your mind." Polycarp said, "Summon them. For us, a change of course from what is better to what is worse cannot be undone, but it is good to move from hardship to what is right." The proconsul said to him again, "If you scorn the beasts and do not change your mind, I will cause you to be consumed by fire." Polycarp said, "You threaten a fire that burns for a time and is soon quenched, for you do not know the fire kept for the impious at the coming judgment and eternal punishment. So why do you delay? Bring whatever you wish."
